title: Loop Polarity Counter
description: Click each link of a four-node causal loop to reveal its polarity, then let the running tally decide whether the loop is reinforcing or balancing.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Causal Loop Diagram Notation and Loop Identification
chapter_title: Causal Loop Diagram Notation and Loop Identification

educational.learningObjective: Given a causal loop diagram, the learner will classify the loop as reinforcing or balancing by counting its opposite-direction links.
prerequisites: Knows what a causal loop diagram is
Can read a + or - polarity on a single link
learningOutcomes: Classify a loop as reinforcing or balancing by counting negative links
Justify each link's polarity in terms of direction of change
Explain why the count, not the number of links, determines loop type
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a written four-link loop and ask for the type plus the count. Check whether they count negative links rather than counting arrows or guessing from the topic.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Click-to-reveal with a running tally and a gated conclusion
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Worked-example fading - the rule is applied by the learner, not demonstrated
pedagogical.feedbackType: Polarity badge, justification sentence, live tally, and a gated R/B reveal
misconceptionsAddressed: That a loop about a positive topic is a reinforcing loop
That more negative links make a loop more balancing
discussionQuestions: Why does an even number of negative links produce reinforcement rather than cancellation?
Can a loop with no negative links ever be balancing?
What happens to the classification if you reverse the direction of one arrow?
